prose.def: The state or time of being a bride; a woman's betrothal or bridal period, used only in the plural.
prose.article: כְּלוּלֹת refers to the condition or season of being a bride, closely related to the common word for 'bride' (כַּלָּה). The ancient Greek translators split in their renderings: one used ἐξακολουθέω ('to follow after') and another used τελείωσις ('completion' or 'perfection'), suggesting the translators understood the word as capturing either the devoted following of a new bride or the fullness of the bridal bond.

prose.article: Col-hozeh is an Israelite proper name appearing 4 times in the book of Nehemiah. The name is composed of two Hebrew elements meaning 'every' and 'seer,' though in context it functions purely as a personal name identifying a man whose son Shallun helped repair Jerusalem's walls, and whose descendant Maaseiah settled in Jerusalem after the exile. The KJV consistently renders it as 'Col-hozeh' without translation, treating it as a name rather than a title.

prose.def: A wide-ranging word for any manufactured object or container, including vessels, tools, weapons, garments, and household goods.
prose.article: כְּלִי covers almost any physical object that has been made or prepared for a purpose — from a cooking pot to a sword to a bag of jewelry. Its breadth is remarkable: the KJV alone renders it with more than twenty different English words, including vessel, weapon, instrument, jewel, and furniture. The Septuagint almost always chooses σκεῦος (226 out of 325 times), a Greek word that similarly covers utensils, equipment, and gear, confirming that ancient readers understood it as a general-purpose word for 'implement.' Its heaviest concentrations are in Exodus, Numbers, and the Chronicles books, reflecting the detailed inventories of tabernacle and temple equipment found there.
